pr_title: nvs: remove unused return code in nvs_sector_close

issue_context.title: Possible issue within nvs_sector_close
issue_context.body:
Hello,

there is an unhandled return value within nvs_sector_close (subsys/fs/nvs/nvs.c line 558). 
For me it's not clear weather the return value is discarded intentionally or if it should actually be returned to the 
caller of the function.
If I compile the code with -Wall enabled I get a -Wunused-but-set-variable  warning at line 542. That's how I discovered this issue.

**Expected behavior**
I'd suggest to either return rc to the caller, e.g.
`rc = nvs_flash_ate_wrt(fs, &close_ate);
if (rc)
  return rc;
`
or casting the return value to void, e.g.
`(void)nvs_flash_ate_wrt(fs, &close_ate);`

**Impact**
This has low priority and no impact to my project.

Best,
Valentin

review_comments:
The return value of `nvs_sector_close` is actually checked at `nvs_write`, where code skips to end when this is not 0.
If this gets discarded the code in `ncs_write` no longer makes sense.
Shouldn't this be rather properly returned by `ncs_sector_close`?

It could return the error code, but this change does not modify the present behavior.

nvs is (should be) resistant to unfinished sector_close writes as it cannot be guaranteed that a close is properly written during a powerdown.
Still there is code that uses the return value, so we either need to do something here or where this is called.

Why ? The return value was always 0 anyhow. A further simplication could be done (this was always the case) but if there ever is a real reason to use the return value it will be much more complex to revert this. This code has been constant for quite some time and I do not see a real reason to change it.
As far as I can tell the NVS is not supported anymore so it is on a death path.
